title: Dispatch: Fix campaign-rule ordering, determinism, and projection provenance (attempt 2)
description:
Dispatch of eshyra-jhpt.1 (attempt 2) — supervisor review fixes on top of attempt 1.

Attempt 1 (eshyra-jhpt.1.1, commit ce3f9a5) delivered packages/core/src/campaign/campaignRules.ts and packages/core/test/campaignRules.test.ts. The structure is sound and is KEPT: the domain/projection split, the move of CampaignRuleProjection/CampaignRulingProjection out of discovery/types.ts into the campaign domain with a re-export for discovery, the validation invariants, and the internal.ts export surface are all correct and must not be reverted. Supervisor review found three defects, reproduced below. Fix exactly these; do not redesign what is working.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.1.2 on branch eshyra-jhpt.1.2, cut from eshyra-jhpt.1.1 (commit ce3f9a5) so attempt 1's work is already present. Work only inside that worktree.

FINDING 1 (SEVERE, correctness) — campaign position ordering is not chronological across sessions.
formatCampaignPosition encodes `cp1~<session>~<turn>~<12-digit ordinal>` and compareCampaignPositions compares that whole string. Session is therefore the PRIMARY sort key, so a later position sorts before an earlier one whenever session ids do not happen to sort lexically in creation order. Reproduced:
    early = { sessionId: 's2',  turnId: 't1', ordinal: 5 }   -> cp1~s2~t1~000000000005
    late  = { sessionId: 's10', turnId: 't1', ordinal: 6 }   -> cp1~s10~t1~000000000006
    compare(early, late) === 1     // positive: the EARLIER position sorts last
The module doc comment claims "Lexical comparison of canonical positions is a total order." It is a total order, but it is the wrong order — it is not chronological. orderCampaignRules is built on this compare, and eshyra-jhpt.3/.4 depend on it for "all and only the rules active at the current position, in deterministic order" and for DM/auditor set parity. A wrong-but-stable order will silently mis-order active rules across session boundaries.
FIX: the monotonic ordinal is the chronological key and must be compared FIRST, with sessionId/turnId as tie-breakers and diagnostic anchors only. Either reorder the encoding so the ordinal leads (e.g. `cp1~<ordinal>~<session>~<turn>`), or compare the parsed struct field-by-field (ordinal, then sessionId, then turnId) instead of comparing formatted strings. State in the doc comment which field is authoritative for chronology and why. Whichever you choose, formatCampaignPosition must stay round-trippable through parseCampaignPosition and stay canonical.

FINDING 2 (correctness/determinism) — compareCampaignPositions uses String.prototype.localeCompare.
localeCompare applies ICU collation in the host's default locale, which is neither codepoint order nor guaranteed stable across environments or Node ICU builds. Reproduced divergences from codepoint order on this machine (node v24.16.0, full ICU):
    'cp1~S1~t~000000000001'.localeCompare('cp1~s1~t~000000000001')  ===  1   (codepoint: -1)
    'cp1~a~t~000000000001'.localeCompare('cp1~B~t~000000000001')    === -1   (codepoint:  1)
Deterministic ordering is a stated acceptance criterion of this bead and of .3/.4; a locale-dependent comparator cannot satisfy it, and a CI or user machine with a different default locale or a small-ICU Node build can order the active rule set differently from a developer machine.
FIX: use explicit codepoint comparison (`a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0`) or numeric/field comparison. Do not use localeCompare anywhere in this ordering path. Note orderCampaignRules also calls `a.ruleIdentity.localeCompare(b.ruleIdentity)` as its final tie-break — same problem, same fix.

FINDING 3 (truthfulness/provenance) — projectCampaignRule fabricates ambiguity provenance for a recurring-question ruling.
For ruleKind 'ruling' with provenance.kind === 'recurring-question' the projection currently emits:
    ambiguityId: `question:${provenance.questionId}`
    selectedInterpretationId: provenance.questionId
No such ambiguity exists in any rules pack and no interpretation was ever selected. The epic's central non-goal is inventing certainty the source does not carry, and ADR 0020 amendment A1 defines the projection's ambiguity id as the LINKED ambiguity id. Synthesizing both fields claims a source linkage and a player selection that never happened. It is currently inert in discovery's resolve path (campaignRuleSeam.ts only marks an ambiguity resolved when the ruling's ambiguityId matches a real pack ambiguity id, which `question:` never will), but it still flows into the packet as campaignRulings[].ambiguityId and will be read downstream as real provenance.
FIX: a recurring-question ruling has no linked ambiguity, so it must project WITHOUT ambiguityId and WITHOUT selectedInterpretationId — i.e. as a plain CampaignRuleProjection carrying ruleKind 'ruling'. Only an 'ambiguity'-provenance ruling may produce a CampaignRulingProjection. Note that packages/core/src/discovery/campaignRuleSeam.ts withRule() currently casts any ruleKind==='ruling' projection to CampaignRulingProjection; check whether that cast becomes unsound under this change and, if it does, report it in your notes and file a bd issue against eshyra-jhpt.3 rather than editing discovery behavior here — this bead is domain-model-only. Do NOT loosen CampaignRulingProjection to make the fabrication type-check.

FINDING 4 (test gap that let 1 and 2 through) — the ordering tests never cross a session or a turn.
packages/core/test/campaignRules.test.ts declares sessionId exactly once, in the `position` helper, so every position in every test shares 'session-1'. The "orders a shuffled active set deterministically" test therefore cannot observe either ordering defect.
FIX: add coverage that would have caught findings 1 and 2 — ordering across sessions with lexically-misleading ids (the s2/s10 case above), ordering across turns within a session, mixed-case and punctuation-bearing session/turn ids, and a shuffled multi-session set whose sorted result is asserted against explicit chronological expectations. Assert the comparator's sign directly, not only the sorted output.

SCOPE
Unchanged from attempt 1: types, invariants, validation, precedence, ordering, projection, and tests only. No SQLite schema, no migration, no storage APIs (.2), no context assembly (.3/.4), no CLI (.5). Do not edit discovery behavior; the re-export in discovery/types.ts stays as attempt 1 left it.

VERIFICATION
`npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root, BEFORE committing (it rewrites files).
notes:
